newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London lower, await Wall St lead.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London lower, await Wall St lead.

text.p: U.S. shares were mostly weaker in cautious late morning trade as European investors remained reluctant to chase prices higher after the Dow's strong advance since the start of the year, dealers said.
Reports that Goldman Sachs equities strategist Abby Cohen had shifted her bullish Wall Street stance dampened market enthusiasm as did the Dow's 47-point slide on Wednesday.
"The Goldman Sachs news has made a few people nervous. Some people here think the Dow is fairly valued at the moment," one market maker said.
"We'll have to wait and see if U.S. investors agree."
The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that Cohen believes the U.S. share market could be entering a trading range after toping the 7,000 level.
News of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping caused only minor ripples in a few selected shares.

Boeing, which historically has captured two-thirds of the Chinese market for commercial jets, was down $3/8 at $109-3/8. Exxon, which has a significant presence in the Chinese energy sector, was down $1/2 at $102-5/8.

Elsewhere, Intel was down $1/2 at $153-3/8 following press reports that Compaq planned to announce later on Thursday it would start selling personal computers priced less than $1,000 using a new chip produced by rival chip-maker Cyrix.
The S&P 500 futures contract on the Globex after-hours trading system was down 0.05 at 814.25 by 1200 GMT, while the March T-bond dipped 5/32 to 113-15/32.
